name: bpf-prog-load
why: bpf(BPF_PROG_LOAD=5) by a non-allowlisted process is the Strategy 1 eBPF-rootkit anchor
source: recorded: strace of ebpf_prog_load_behavioral.c -- bpf(5, attr, 0x90). a2 is sizeof(union bpf_attr)=0x90 (the atomic passes sizeof(*attr)); exit is the decimal prog fd

name: bpf-prog-load-dropper
why: a second non-allowlisted loader (a shell-spawned binary) loading a program is the same anchor; the comm value must not matter beyond the allowlist
source: synthetic: a dropper loading an eBPF program; a2 is sizeof(union bpf_attr)=0x90

name: bpf-map-create
why: bpf(BPF_MAP_CREATE=0) is the setup step the atomic issues just before the load; it is not itself a program load, so the a0 command constraint must hold
source: recorded: strace of ebpf_prog_load_behavioral.c -- bpf(0, attr, 0x90) before the load

name: bpf-prog-attach
why: bpf(BPF_PROG_ATTACH=8) attaches an already-loaded program; the load (a0=5) is the anchored step, so attach alone must not fire
source: synthetic: a PROG_ATTACH command; a2 is sizeof(union bpf_attr)=0x90

name: ioctl-on-fd5-not-bpf
why: auditd logs bpf()'s a0 as the command, but for ioctl() a0 is the fd number; an ioctl on fd 5 holds the a0=5 atom yet is not the bpf syscall. This is the realistic high-volume look-alike in this schema, so the bpf syscall anchor must be load-bearing
source: synthetic: an ordinary ioctl on fd 5 (a0 collides with BPF_PROG_LOAD=5)

name: bpftool-allowlisted
why: bpftool loads programs legitimately; the comm allowlist alone must suppress it
source: synthetic: bpftool prog load; a2 is sizeof(union bpf_attr)=0x90

name: systemd-allowlisted
why: systemd loads eBPF for cgroup/BPF-LSM programs at boot; the system-controller identity must be filtered
source: synthetic: systemd (pid 1) loading a cgroup eBPF program; a2 is sizeof(union bpf_attr)=0x90

name: unrelated-write
why: an ordinary ioctl(fd, TCGETS) by a routine process: an audited syscall (atomic.rules records ioctl) that shares neither the anchored syscall nor its arguments -- a sanity floor that must stay quiet
source: synthetic: a routine ioctl(TCGETS), an audited high-volume syscall used as a non-firing floor

name: runc-device-filter-load-filtered
why: runc loads its cgroup-v2 device-filter program (BPF_PROG_TYPE_CGROUP_DEVICE) for every container it creates; the runc entry of runtime_images suppresses it (the old comm allowlist had no runc entry). Rootful runc runs as root with no login uid, which the runc entry's euid condition requires
source: runc v1.1.12 libcontainer/cgroups/ebpf/ebpf_linux.go (ebpf.NewProgram for the device filter); events as in the benign corpus docker-run template

name: snap-confine-device-cgroup-load-filtered
why: snap-confine loads the snap's device-cgroup BPF program on a snap launch; the snap-confine entry of runtime_images suppresses it
source: snapd cmd/libsnap-confine-private/device-cgroup-support.c: bpf_load_prog(BPF_PROG_TYPE_CGROUP_DEVICE, ...); exe as in the benign corpus snap-confine template

name: runc-path-with-other-comm
why: a program load from a binary at a runc path whose comm is not runc (for example a loader dropped at /usr/bin/runc inside a container, which the kernel logs relative to the container's root) still fires: the runc entry needs both the comm and the path
source: synthetic: bpf(BPF_PROG_LOAD) with comm loader, exe /usr/bin/runc

name: ldpreload-into-runc-socket-filter-as-user
why: with kernel.unprivileged_bpf_disabled=0 an unprivileged user can load a socket-filter program (the path of verifier privilege escalations); run inside /usr/bin/runc with LD_PRELOAD, the load keeps comm runc and exe /usr/bin/runc but carries the user's euid, so the runc entry (euid 0) does not suppress it. The rule without the euid condition suppressed this
source: synthetic from recorded mechanism: LD_PRELOAD into the non-setuid /usr/bin/runc keeps its comm and exe (recorded as uid 65534, see T1620 ldpreload-into-runc-as-exe-known-miss); linux v6.8 kernel/bpf/syscall.c bpf_prog_load(): only SOCKET_FILTER and CGROUP_SKB load without bpf_capable(), and only when unprivileged_bpf_disabled is 0

name: runc-device-filter-root-euid-filtered
why: `docker run` through a rootful runc at /usr/sbin/runc (the Debian/Ubuntu runc package path) loads its cgroup-v2 device filter as root: euid 0 is what the runc entry needs beyond comm and exe, and the same load with an unprivileged euid fires (see ldpreload-into-runc-socket-filter-as-user). Rootless runc issues BPF_PROG_QUERY first, which fails without CAP_NET_ADMIN, and never loads, so the condition costs no rootless noise
source: runc v1.1.12 libcontainer/cgroups/ebpf/ebpf_linux.go LoadAttachCgroupDeviceFilter (findAttachedCgroupDeviceFilters' BPF_PROG_QUERY error returns before ebpf.NewProgram) and cgroups/fs2/fs2.go (setDevices errors ignored when Rootless); linux v6.8 kernel/bpf/syscall.c bpf_prog_query() (CAP_NET_ADMIN)

name: snap-confine-user-launch-filtered
why: a user launching a snap with the distribution's snapd >= 2.70, which installs /usr/lib/snapd/snap-confine with file capabilities, so it keeps the caller's uid and euid (1000): snap-confine loads the device-cgroup program, and the snap-confine entry has no euid condition, so a user's launch stays filtered. An unprivileged user cannot inject into it: the capability gain (or, before snapd 2.70, set-user-ID root) puts it in secure-execution mode (AT_SECURE: ld.so ignores an LD_PRELOAD path) and makes it non-dumpable, so the user cannot ptrace it
source: snapd 2.70 cmd/Makefile.am and packaging/ubuntu-16.04/snapd.postinst (setcap from snap-confine.caps; 2.69 and earlier: chmod 4755); linux v6.8 security/commoncap.c cap_bprm_creds_from_file (secureexec for a set-user-ID exec or when a non-root caller gains permitted capabilities); ld.so(8) secure-execution mode; kernel/ptrace.c __ptrace_may_access

name: snap-confine-path-in-user-namespace-known-miss
why: KNOWN MISS (an unprivileged program load that the snap-confine entry suppresses): with kernel.unprivileged_bpf_disabled=0, a user creates a user and mount namespace (unshare -rmpf), mounts a tmpfs, places their own loader at /snap/snapd/1/usr/lib/snapd/snap-confine and runs it from there (chroot). The kernel logs exe relative to the process's root and mounts, so its BPF_PROG_LOAD of a socket filter carries that path, and auditd logs the user's host uid and euid (65534), the same ids a snap-confine from snapd >= 2.70 (file capabilities) has. The snap-confine entry matches the path alone, so it suppresses the load. Remove the entry on hosts without snapd. Labelled filtered because that is what the rule does with it
source: recorded by the reviewer: unshare -rmpf + tmpfs + chroot as uid 65534 (uid_map 0 65534 1); /proc/<pid>/exe and the audit exe were /snap/snapd/1/usr/lib/snapd/snap-confine; linux v6.8 kernel/bpf/syscall.c bpf_prog_load() (SOCKET_FILTER loads without bpf_capable() when unprivileged_bpf_disabled is 0)
